s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive facial weakness with bilateral lower motor neuron involvement in a patient with a history of chemotherapy
salient_findings: Bilateral lower motor neuron facial muscle weakness
key_facts: Received four cycles of Folfirinox chemotherapy without significant response
Developed bilateral facial drooping after 20 cycles of combined therapy and 16 additional cycles of nab-paclitaxel alone
Experienced grade 1 peripheral neuropathy which remained stable while taking vitamin B6 supplements
Developed severe edema due to capillary leak which led to discontinuation of gemcitabine
Neurological evaluation revealed bilateral lower motor neuron facial muscle weakness
MRI Brain revealed bilateral facial nerve enhancement compatible with bilateral facial neuritis

shortlist.label: Facial neuritis
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral facial nerve enhancement on MRI Brain

shortlist.label: Paraneoplastic syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: History of pancreatic adenocarcinoma and progressive facial weakness

shortlist.label: Chemotherapy-induced neuropathy
shortlist.why_kept: History of chemotherapy and development of bilateral facial drooping

shortlist.label: Guillain-Barré syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral lower motor neuron facial muscle weakness

shortlist.label: Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: History of cancer and progressive muscle weakness

raw.rationale: Bilateral facial nerve enhancement on MRI Brain compatible with bilateral facial neuritis, without evidence of intracranial or leptomeningeal malignancy, directly explains the patient's symptoms of bilateral facial drooping, inability to close her eyelids, and difficulty raising her eyebrows

rejected.label: Paraneoplastic syndrome
rejected.why: No evidence of other systemic symptoms or autoantibodies typically associated with paraneoplastic syndromes

rejected.label: Chemotherapy-induced neuropathy
rejected.why: Patient's symptoms are localized to the facial nerves, and grade 1 peripheral neuropathy was stable with vitamin B6 supplements

rejected.label: Guillain-Barré syndrome
rejected.why: Lack of rapid progression and absence of other neurological deficits, with normal laboratory tests including creatine kinase

rejected.label: Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome
rejected.why: No evidence of proximal muscle weakness, and normal serological tests

gold: Bilateral facial nerve palsy induced by nab-paclitaxel
